steps.instruction: Trim the stem ends of the okra and cut into pieces about 2.5cm long. Check for any insect damage as you cut.
Heat the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the cinnamon stick, curry leaves, and garlic, and stir-fry for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the sliced onion and cook until it becomes tender, about 2-3 minutes. Add the chopped tomato and green chillies, and cook for another 1-2 minutes.
Add the cumin powder, turmeric, and curry powder. Mix well with the other ingredients in the pan.
Add the okra pieces and stir-fry over fairly high heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring frequently. Add the salt while stirring.

Pour in the thin coconut milk first, then the thick coconut milk, mixing carefully. Cook uncovered over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for about 6-8 minutes, until the okra is just tender -- it should retain a slight bite and bright green colour, so avoid overcooking. Cooking uncovered helps preserve the colour.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice.

source_site: rasakama.wordpress.com, cross-checked against anomaskitchen.com, cookveggielicious.com, and katylanka.com for technique consistency
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 5+ independent sources; strong agreement on cooking uncovered to preserve okra's green colour and avoid mushiness
notes: Most sources agree this dish should be cooked uncovered once the coconut milk is added, both to preserve the okra's bright green colour and to control its natural sliminess -- covering the pot traps steam and tends to make the dish duller and softer than desired. Unlike many other vegetable curries in this collection, bandakka curry traditionally contains no red chilli powder, relying instead on green chillies for heat; it is meant to be one of the milder dishes on the table, often paired with a spicier meat, fish, or dry-fish curry.
